controls.why: 0002 is recorded and row 42 has body_len NULL, so only the 'backfilled' part of card leg (a) breaks; the original rows keep their id and body, which keeps (b), and the next apply only builds 0003's index and exits 0, which keeps (c).
With the start's record, schema and rows plus a trigger that aborts every UPDATE, (a) and (b) hold and only card leg (c) breaks, because the next apply fails at 0002's backfill.

`mark -m 0003` records 0003 with no index, which breaks card leg (a); the next apply then skips 0003 and never makes the index, so card leg (c) ('leaves the final schema') breaks too, as friction row 6 itself admits.

An extra index on notes with record {0001} breaks neither card (a) (0001's change is all there) nor (b); at most it touches (c)'s 'final schema', so it does not break the card leg its schema leg stands for.
